THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR FINAL HEARING, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT 1.

This appeal is preferred by the owner of the offending vehicle being aggrieved by the judgment and award passed by the MACT, Court of Small Causes, Bengaluru City in MVC No.1223/2011 dated 27.08.2012.

sentences.text: This appeal is premised on the ground that the judgment and award of the Tribunal is erroneous, perverse and the same deserves to be set aside.
2. Parties are referred to as they are cited before the Tribunal.

3. Brief facts of the case leading to the filing of this petition are as under :
That on 26.05.2010 at 09.50 a.m. when the claimant was traveling on the tractor trailer bearing No.KA-11-T-3033, KA- 11-T-7558 as a loader with bricks, the vehicle being driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner, took a sudden turn in high speed, due to which the tractor trailer lost control and turned turtle; as a result of which the claimant, who was sitting in the tractor trailer, fell down and sustained injuries to himself.
Thereafter, he was shifted to the Government hospital.

He took treatment and underwent certain medical emergency operation and spent exorbitant amount towards medical treatment, hence the claimant filed claim petition against the owner and insurer of the tractor and trailer.

The Tribunal allowed the claim petition awarding compensation of Rs.4,31,400/-, fastening the liability on respondent No.1/ owner of the vehicle thereby absolving respondent No.2-insurer from liability to pay compensation, hence, Respondent No.1 is in appeal.

4. It is the contention of the learned counsel appearing for the appellant-owner that the Tribunal has committed an error in fastening the liability as against the owner of the offending vehicle and absolving and dismissing the claim petition as against respondent No.2-Insurance Company.

He further contends that even though the plea is taken that the claimant was traveling in the tractor and trailer as a fare paid passenger, it is case of the claimant that he was a loader of the goods and was traveling along with the goods.

Therefore, the policy being in force, it is incumbent upon the insurance company to pay compensation and the liability ought to have been fastened on the insurance company rather than the owner of the offending vehicle.
It is also the contention of the learned counsel that the compensation awarded to the claimant by the Tribunal is on the higher side and the same requires to be reduced and modified.
Accordingly, he seeks to allow the appeal.

sentences.text: Per contra, learned counsel representing the Insurance Company is present before the Court and vehemently contends that the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal is correct as there is no illegality or perversity committed by the Tribunal in fastening the liability against the owner of the offending vehicle.

It is an admitted fact that policy was insured for the use of tractor trailer- agricultural purpose whereas, the same was used for commercial purpose for transporting certain bricks, which is not in dispute.
Therefore, there is a clear breach and fundamental breach of violation of the terms and conditions of the policy.
Thereby the Tribunal, having upheld this contention by the Insurance Company, has rightly fastened the liability as against the owner of the offending vehicle which does not call for interference.
On these grounds, he seeks to dismiss the appeal.
6. There is no representation on behalf of the counsel for the respondent No.1-claimant.

7. Having heard learned counsel for both the parties, the point that arise for consideration before this Court are :
i) Whether the appellant/owner of the offending vehicle has made out a case for interference for modification of the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal ?
ii) What order ?
8.

It is not in dispute that on 26.5.2010 at 9.50 a.m. when the claimant was traveling on the tractor trailer bearing No. KA-11- T-3033, KA-11-T-7558 as a loader with bricks, the vehicle being driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner, took a sudden turn in high speed due to which the tractor-trailer lost control and turned turtle; as a result of which the claimant, who was sitting in the tractor trailer, fell down and sustained injuries to himself.
Thereafter, he was shifted to the Government hospital.
He took treatment and underwent certain medical emergency operation and spent exorbitant huge amount towards medical treatment.

The occurrence of the accident,
involvement of the vehicle, injuries sustained by the claimant are all not disputed by the respondents before the Tribunal.
However, the same are proved and established by producing exhibits P1 to P9, police records and medical records.

The policy of insurance has been produced at Ex.R1.
9.

The contention of the learned counsel for the owner of the offending vehicle, I am afraid, cannot be accepted for the reason that, admittedly the policy was issued by the Insurance Company for use of the vehicle for agricultural purpose.

Admittedly, in the present case, it was used for commercial purposes for transporting certain bricks and the claimant who was an inmate of the tractor trailer,
sitting on the bricks loaded on the trailer, due to control being lost by the driver of the tractor, he fell down and sustained injuries.

The Tribunal has analysed the injuries sustained by the claimant and has awarded compensation on the basis of the injuries sustained which does not call for much interference as no legal grounds are made to interfere with the award of compensation, so also with regard to the income, age and multiplier adopted by the Tribunal.
The only point of argument that is canvassed by the owner of the offending vehicle is that the liability is to be fixed on the Insurance Company.

I am afraid the same cannot be accepted as it is far fetched in view of the admission by Channegowda vs Ashoka C M on 19 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102972748/
3 the claimant as well as respondents and the documents produced by the jurisdictional police that the claimant was travelling on the bricks loaded on the tractor trailer which met with the accident.
Even according to the policy, the vehicle in question was to be used for agricultural purpose and not for any other purpose viz.commercial use.

The owner of the offending vehicle having used the tractor trailer for commercial purpose for transporting bricks from one place to another is a fundamental breach of the terms and conditions of the policy which would absolve the liability of the Insurance Company and has to be fastened on the owner for having committed the breach.

10. Under such circumstances, I do not find much merit or any cogent piece of evidence placed before the Court to accept the theory put forth by the learned counsel for the offending vehicle/appellant.
Hence, I do not find any merit in the matter to interfere with the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal.

11. Accordingly, I pass the following order :
ORDER i) Appeal is dismissed as devoid of merits.

The judgment and award passed by the Tribunal in MVC No.1223/2011 dated 27.8.2012 is sustained and upheld;
ii) The amount in dispute shall be transmitted to the jurisdictional Tribunal forthwith.

The entire compensation amount shall be paid by respondent No.1/owner of the offending vehicle-appellant herein to the claimant from the date of filing the petition till the date of realisation with interest at 6% p.a.
The entire amount of compensation shall be paid within a period of 6 weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.
All other terms and conditions stipulated by the Tribunal is retained and not interfered.
The original trial Court records be sent to the jurisdictional tribunal forthwith.
